findings.reason: it moves the new renderer to a shared owner and adds the two code-domain call sites to §14's scope (or forces the plan to say in its text why the code-domain copies are deliberately left forked).
findings.text: §14 adds one root-scope renderer in the paths module and consolidates the five paths sites, but the identical predicate is already spelled twice more in imas_codex/discovery/code/graph_ops.py:140 and graph_ops.py:565 (`AND ANY(pre IN $prefixes WHERE p.path STARTS WITH pre)`), and §14 re-runs that same code scan with the same three prefixes, so the two domains keep parallel implementations of one predicate that can drift — the plan's own rule ("must not be spelled a sixth time") is unmet and the honest home for the renderer is the shared base module that already owns the reset (imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py), reachable by both domains

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the change deepens rather than spreads: one module-level renderer hides the root-scope Cypher behind a single interface, replacing five inline spellings; the reset-spec edit is data (a field added to `clear_fields`), not new surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the "under these roots" predicate is already spelled seven times (five in imas_codex/discovery/paths/parallel.py:483,539,596,714,794 and two in imas_codex/discovery/code/graph_ops.py:140,565), and §14 routes only the five paths sites through a new renderer placed in the paths module, leaving the code-domain pair as a forked copy of the same predicate.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §14 adds no CLI option and no MCP view (it reuses the existing `--root` and `--reset-to`), and it names the merge its one new function performs (the five inline spellings into one, "must not be spelled a sixth time"), so its single added definition is accounted for in its own text.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan named the mechanism it extends for each change and every citation resolves to the code it names: `reset_to_status` / `PATH_RESET_SPECS` with `extra_filter`/`extra_params` (imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py:59-127,240-255), the signals-command precedent for a scoped reset (imas_codex/cli/discover/signals.py), the unfiltered paths call (imas_codex/cli/discover/paths.py:248), and the five inline root clauses (imas_codex/discovery/paths/parallel.py:483,539,596,714,794).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no wrapper is introduced. §14 extends the existing owner `reset_to_status` through the `extra_filter`/`extra_params` parameters it already exposes (reset.py:63-64) and the claim functions through their existing `root_filter` argument, which the plan states explicitly rather than adding a parallel layer.
